teaching.hint: Which operator could be the final one evaluated in a fully parenthesized expression?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Every full expression tree has one root operator that separates independent left and right subexpressions.
solution_outline.approach: For each operator position, obtain all values from its left and right ranges, combine every pair using that operator, and concatenate the results. Memoize repeated ranges.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A range state stores the list of values for all parenthesizations of exactly that range, including multiplicity; a number-only range has its one literal value.
solution_outline.correctness: Every parenthesization has exactly one final operator and one left/right parenthesization pair. Enumerating all splits and pairings therefore lists every structural result exactly once; equal values remain duplicated.
solution_outline.complexity: Time and storage scale with all values materialized across subranges and are exponential in the number of operators in the worst case; the 20-character and 10,000-result bounds keep this feasible.
solution_outline.pitfall: Using a set loses required duplicate results from distinct expression trees.

common_wrong_turns: Apply ordinary precedence instead of all groupings
Split multi-digit numbers as single digits
source_fidelity_notes: Explicitly retained output multiplicity and multi-digit input numbers; removed lengthy enumerated output.
